_readme: Waiting-room notes shown while media is really waiting (loading / seeking / buffering / network stalled). Edit freely: add lines, themes, acronyms. Rules: keep every line under ~90 characters; never claim the media is ready or that something was fixed (the elapsed timer and the real status are always shown beside the joke); no real quotes from copyrighted works or real people, everything here is original.

any.long: Please Observe Patient Content Of Reels Nearly Nearby
Fetching Lots Of Unrelated Fuzzy Frames
Bafflingly Under-powered Flux Field Emitting Resonance
Sluggish Transmission Attempting To Initiate Connection

seeking.long: Reel Eventually Wound, Is Nearly Done

buffering.long: Transmission Of A Slightly Toasty Track

themes.label: Wires
lines: Untangling the wires. There were more knots than wires.
Our best cable is currently doing yoga. Please hold.
Plugging it in the other way around. Third time lucky.
A wire has been located behind the couch. Following it.
Checking the cable for kinks. It has a lot of feelings.
The signal is taking the scenic route through the cables.
Blowing dust out of the connector, like a gentleman.
Someone tripped on the extension cord. Not naming names.
Wiggling the antenna until the picture likes us again.
Duct-taping the cable to the wall. Very professional.

themes.label: Rats
lines: A rat is chewing on the cable. We are negotiating with cheese.
The rat union has called a lunch break mid-transmission.
Rat spotted on the line. It says it is 'just reviewing the bandwidth'.
Tiny rat carrying one packet at a time. Very committed.
The rat found the good cable. The cable is now a snack.
Rat supervisor says the delay is 'within snack tolerances'.
Offering the rat a cracker for a faster connection.
The rats are rewiring this. They have not read the manual.
A very small rat is pushing the buffer uphill.
Rat in the router. It looks happy. We are not.

themes.label: VHS
lines: Taking the tape out of the box. The box fought back.
Peeling the 'BE KIND, REWIND' sticker off the old tape.
Blowing on the cartridge, because that always worked.
Slotting the tape in. It goes in sideways. Always sideways.
Fast-forwarding past the trailers nobody asked for.
Tracking is a bit off. Twisting the little knob.
Rewinding, because somebody did not rewind last time.
The tape is in the shop's 'new releases' pile. Walking there.
Checking if the label says 'Do Not Tape Over'. It does.
Cleaning the heads with a wet cloth and a prayer.

themes.label: VCR era
lines: Warming up the VCR. The clock is blinking 12:00 as tradition demands.
Loading the VCR era. Please keep your arms inside the living room.
Pressing PLAY and STOP at the same time, for luck.
The remote needs new batteries. Borrowing two from the smoke alarm.
Setting the timer to record. It is set to record Tuesday forever.
Hooking up the yellow, white, and red plugs. Pretty sure that is right.
Channel 3 or 4? Flipping the little switch to find out.
Rolling a fresh pack of static into the screen.
Waiting for the TV to find its blue screen. It always finds it.
The VCR is making the noise. That is the good noise.

themes.label: Old modem
lines: Dialing in. Please do not pick up the phone.
The modem is singing its little song of progress.
Handshaking with Archive. It has not yet decided to shake back.
Everyone in the house is asked to please stay off the phone line.
Downloading the image one stripe at a time, the old way.
Squeaks, hisses and beeps. This is the sound of ambition.
Asking the dial tone for permission to continue.
Reaching the internet by carrier pigeon. The pigeon is stretching.

themes.label: The Archive
lines: The librarian has gone to the very back shelf for this one.
Archive is climbing a tall ladder. We can hear the ladder.
A librarian is blowing dust off the box. Dust is winning.
They keep the good reels in the cellar. Cellar stairs are steep.
Looking in the 'miscellaneous' drawer, which is the whole building.
The librarian said 'one moment' eleven seconds ago. Honouring it.
Reel located. Reel is under another reel. Reel-ception.
Checking out your item. Library card was in the other coat.

themes.label: Bytes
lines: Bytes are lining up politely. A few are cutting.
Packing the bytes into very small suitcases.
The bytes are carpooling. One is still looking for its shoes.
Counting the ones and zeroes. Twice, to be sure.
A bit fell off the truck. Sending out a very small search party.
Inflating the buffer. Do not pop the buffer.
The packets left on time. The road did not.
Ferrying audio across the internet one bucket at a time.

themes.label: Snack break
lines: Good time for popcorn. We will shout when the show is ready.
Stretch break! Roll the shoulders, look out the window.
A sip of something warm is highly recommended.
Tip: seeking far ahead takes a bit longer than seeking near.
Tip: stay put after a jump and the next stretch loads faster.
The show will begin the moment it begins. Not before.
Fun fact: patience has never once made the video slower.

themes.label: Retro tech
lines: Waking up the hamsters on the wheel inside the modem...
Rats are currently chewing through the high-voltage wires out back...
Blowing dust out of the VCR cartridge and crossing our fingers...
Rewinding the magnetic tape with a standard yellow pencil...
Adjusting the bunny-ear antennas for better analog reception...
Waiting for the dial-up modem to finish making its strange robot noises...
Loading pixels one by one from the floppy disk box...
Brushing crumb-chewers away from the motherboard...
Packing the VHS video back out of the dusty cardboard box...
Thumping the top of the monitor to fix horizontal tracking...
Waiting for the vacuum tubes to warm up to operating temperature...

slow: Still waiting. The rat is asking for a raise.
Archive is taking its sweet time. We are taking ours too.
Still on it. The kettle has boiled and re-boiled.
Longer than usual. Somewhere a cable is being very dramatic.
No, it did not forget you. It is just walking slowly.
This is the long way round. You may press Retry if you like.
quotes: Good things come to those who wait, and slightly better things to those who rewind.
A buffer is just a very patient hug.
Every great show begins with a small pause and a smaller rat.
The wire is long, but the song is longer.
Slow internet builds character. And snacks.
Somewhere a reel is spinning just for you.
Tape hiss is the sound of the past clearing its throat.
Even the fastest cable has a Monday.
A watched progress bar never moves. Look at the picture on the wall instead.
The best sound in the world is the click right before the music starts.
